transcript:
Header: 2026-02-25 14:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Maria Lopez (EdgeScale - Head of ML), Daniel Kim (EdgeScale - SRE), Lina Park (EdgeScale - Product), Tom Evans (EdgeScale - CTO), Jia Wu (EdgeScale - ML Eng)

Summary (auto): quick review of last week's runs, focused on latency/throughput numbers vs baseline provider, discuss tuning knobs and next steps.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call, then priya will walk through the numbers.
00:12 Maria Lopez: thanks alex, yeah we pulled the updated sheet earlier, looks promising, excited to hear the breakdown.
00:20 Priya Nair: cool, slide one — uh so we ran the same 10k synthetic queries against your model artifacts, same prompt set, we tested on our GPU-optimized runtime (A100 equiv) with two configs: default and quantized int8 plus batching. Baseline provider numbers were from your shared spreadsheet last week.
00:45 Jia Wu: just to confirm — baseline was 80 qps peak and p99 420ms?
00:51 Priya Nair: yep that's what you gave, baseline peak throughput ~80 qps, p50 ~75ms, p99 ~420ms. Our runs showed: default config peak 120 qps, p50 55ms, p99 360ms. With batch=8 + int8 quant we pushed peak to 210 qps, p50 30ms, p99 300ms.
01:18 Daniel Kim: those are nice on median but p99 still a delta vs our SLO of 200ms. Any ideas on the tail?
01:25 Priya Nair: right, so tail is workload-dependent, we saw outliers caused by long-context KV cache misses and occasional batch misalignment. Two levers: 1) warm prefix cache (we can pre-warm common prefixes), 2) smaller latency-priority batch sizes for real-time routes, and 3) routing some requests to a lower-latency model variant.
01:49 Tom Evans: warm prefix cache sounds interesting, how much engineering overhead is that?
01:54 Priya Nair: minimal — runtime supports prefix/KV caching, we can seed the cache during rollout or use a tiny warmup traffic shim. Priya: (laughs) sorry, i said priya twice.
02:05 Alex Chen: (brief) Also worth noting, on average the quantized path reduces token compute cost by ~2.5x which affects cost projections for Dedicated pilot.
02:18 Lina Park: cost is important, but continuity is more important — we need stable tails during peak.
02:23 Maria Lopez: can we re-run the test with batch size tuned per route? Some of our calls are very short, others long.
02:31 Priya Nair: yes we planned per-route profiling; for this week we can run: route A batch=4 latency-priority, route B batch=12 throughput-priority. That should reduce mixed-workload tail.
02:44 Jia Wu: any difference between A100 equiv and T4-like cards? Our prod infra uses mixed instances.
02:50 Priya Nair: good question — throughput scales down and quant benefits are smaller on T4; we can provide a mixed-hardware run. For now these numbers are on A100-style.
03:05 Daniel Kim: security question — we need details on KMS integration and audit logs for Private deployment. You mentioned KMS earlier.
03:12 Sam Ortiz: yep, we'll send the VPC/KMS runbook. Short answer: we support customer KMS keys for model artifacts and request logs, plus audit logging for inference requests. We'll put links in the deck.
03:25 Maria Lopez: required compliance: SOC2 + ISO27001. Is that covered for Hosted? For Private we'll need certificates.
03:32 Alex Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II, ISO in progress — for Private we can provide self-host package and support for your compliance reviewers. I'll share the compliance packet after the call.
03:44 Priya Nair: back to latency, one more datapoint: p99 spikes often correlate with GC spikes in your model server when we used default JVM-ish runtimes — i mean some teams have observed memory compaction effects with long sequences. For us the inference engine uses continuous KV cache with low GC overhead, but we'll need your exact payloads to reproduce.
04:08 Maria Lopez: ok we'll share 50k representative requests anonymized.
04:13 Alex Chen: great — that's actually an action item.
04:20 Priya Nair: notes on methodology: we used closed-loop load generator with Poisson arrivals, 99%ile computed on request completion times, warmup 5 minutes. We attached full logs in the sheet. There may be small transcription or label mismatches in metric names vs your internal naming.
04:43 Jia Wu: in the sheet i saw a row labeled p95 that looked like p99 in other tools, can you double-check?
04:48 Priya Nair: sure, we'll normalize the labels.
04:52 Tom Evans: curious — what about autoscaling? Baseline provider auto scaled poorly for us, high cold-start. How's Redwood's burst behaviour?
05:02 Priya Nair: autoscale uses predictive scaling plus fast warm pools; cold start is typically under 200ms for queued requests to spin a worker on Dedicated depending on model size. For strict SLOs we recommend reserved pool with burst headroom.
05:18 Daniel Kim: do you have any numbers on cold-start for the quantized int8 path?
05:24 Priya Nair: quantized kernels tend to load slightly faster because memory footprint is smaller; cold-start measured 120-180ms on our lab runs for this model. We'll add that to the sheet.
05:40 Alex Chen: ok moving on — questions from procurement side, pricing for Dedicated pilot?
05:45 Maria Lopez: yeah we need a ballpark to budget for next quarter.
05:49 Alex Chen: i'll send a dedicated pilot estimate based on the quantized throughput numbers — gives more realistic unit-cost, feel free to push back. Pricing doc will include burst options and 99th tail mitigation SLA credits.
06:02 Lina Park: regarding integration, any networking constraints for Private? We run in an air-gapped segment for a subset of services.
06:10 Sam Ortiz: Private on-prem can be configured for air-gapped installs; tradeoffs are some management features are offline but core inference and tracing still work. We'll pair you with a solutions engineer for install checklist.
06:22 Maria Lopez: great. next — we wanted to validate accuracy/regression when we quantize. How bad was quality loss?
06:29 Priya Nair: on our evaluation harness, int8 quant had negligible top-level regression on token-level logprobs for your prompt set, delta <0.8% ROUGE-like metric. We do recommend running your evals; results can vary by model and prompt.
06:45 Jia Wu: can we run A/B tests during pilot to validate quality under real traffic?
06:49 Alex Chen: absolutely, the rollout supports canary A/B and automatic fallback to non-quantized if quality drops.
06:56 Maria Lopez: ok good.
07:00 Priya Nair: quick note on observability — we included per-token latency traces and per-route cost breakdowns in the sheet. That should help decide which routes to quantize.
07:12 Daniel Kim: i saw a spike at 11:12 in the logs, looks correlated with batch misalignment; any fix for alignment?
07:20 Priya Nair: yes, runtime supports request padding and alignment strategies; we can force per-route alignment or use adaptive packer that waits 5-10ms for a packing window. There's a tradeoff of median latency vs throughput.
07:34 Tom Evans: sounds like we need a knob to control alignment window per route, agreed.
07:40 Priya Nair: we can expose that in the pilot.
07:44 Alex Chen: ok -- before we wrap, let's confirm concrete next steps and owners.
07:50 Maria Lopez: quick recap, please.
07:52 Alex Chen: action recap: Priya will rerun microbench with batch=8 and int8 quant and add mixed-hardware runs; Priya will add cold-start numbers and alignment window tests. Maria will provide anonymized 50k sample and tail targets. Alex will share SOC2/ISO docs and pricing. Sam will schedule the VPC/KMS deep-dive for next Wednesday. We'll reconvene same time next week to review reruns.
08:20 Maria Lopez: perfect. Thanks everyone.
08:23 Alex Chen: thanks all, meeting adjourned.
